svg.title: OspreyFlow, level 1
svg.desc: Every component of an OspreyFlow deployment by tier, with the technology each is built on, the ports between the Conduit and the Vault, the identity provider and reporting beside them, and what each mode runs on.
svg.text: OspreyFlow at level 1: every component, and what it is built with
As of v0.4.3; versions are those the release pins. Small and Enterprise use the cloud's managed services (last row).
The only published port: 443 (and 80 for certificates) on Small and Enterprise; 80 on
127.0.0.1 on Lite. It routes the deployment's address, id. (sign-in) and bi. (dashboards).
HTTPS · REST /v1 (JSON) · server-sent events for progress · WebSocket change stream (30-second ticket)
a bearer JWT on every call
Everything between tiers crosses a named port. A BI tool never reads the Vault:
it reads figures the Conduit counted for a named dashboard identity.
Helm chart on EKS or AKS
S3 or Blob; EFS or Files
Outside the deployment, each only when switched on: a hosted model provider (only datasets cleared for it),
online map tiles, mail, your organisation's sign-in. Every container sits on an internal network with no route
out; one joins the egress network only for the feature that needs it.
